qt: to the Commission Tom Vandendriessche (PfE), András László (PfE), Elisabeth Dieringer (PfE), Dominik Tarczyński (ECR), Tomasz Froelich (ESN), Petra Steger (PfE), Roman Haider (PfE), Irmhild Boßdorf (ESN), Marc Jongen (ESN), Gerolf Annemans (PfE), Silvia Sardone (PfE), Barbara Bonte (PfE), Roberto Vannacci (ESN), Mary Khan (ESN), Fabrice Leggeri (PfE), Anna Bryłka (PfE), Mélanie Disdier (PfE), Milan Uhrík (ESN), Volker Schnurrbusch (ESN), Branko Grims (NI), Ondřej Knotek (PfE), Jaak Madison (ECR), Tiago Moreira de Sá (PfE) Subject:

The EU anti-racism strategy 2026–2030 is built on the death of George Floyd and the Black Lives Matter movement. That origin matters, as it imports an American racial narrative into EU policy: racism flows in one direction only, with minorities as victims and white citizens as perpetrators. That double standard is written into the strategy itself. It names anti-Black racism, antigypsyism, antisemitism, anti-Asian racism and anti-Muslim hatred. White Europeans as potential victims: absent. By design. This asymmetry is not theoretical. It is deadly. The Henry Nowak case shows where this logic ends: a white student fatally stabbed, then handcuffed after his attacker falsely invoked racism. The accusation overruled reality. A doctrine designed to fight discrimination produced the opposite: unequal credibility before the law, at the cost of a life. 1.
What empirical evidence demonstrates that EU-supported anti-racism training does not create credibility presumptions based on skin colour?
Will the Commission include safeguards against weaponised racism accusations in its upcoming policing compendium?
Will the Commission revise the EU anti-racism strategy 2026–2030 to guarantee equal protection for all citizens regardless of skin colour?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.10.2026) The Anti-Racism Strategy 2026–20301 aims to create a more equal and inclusive EU by tackling racism in all its forms. It focuses on enforcing anti-discrimination legislation, addressing societal barriers in areas such as education, employment, healthcare and housing, and strengthening social cohesion. The Strategy also responds to the European Parliament’s call for a long-term approach to combating racism and promotes equal treatment of all people living in the EU regardless of skin colour2. The stakeholders consulted in the preparation of the Anti-Racism Strategy underlined the need for comprehensive training programmes for law enforcement authorities and greater transparency and accountability within law enforcement agencies. To provide further guidance to Member States, the Commission will compile a compendium of good practices to prevent discriminatory profiling practices.
